summary: Etomidate is an ultrashort-acting imidazole IV anesthetic used for induction and brief procedural sedation, prized for hemodynamic stability with minimal cardiac depression. Typical induction dose is 0.3 mg/kg IV. Onset is within 1 minute and duration is 3-5 minutes. Key adverse effects are pain on injection, myoclonus, postoperative nausea/vomiting, and dose-dependent adrenocortical suppression - which precludes continuous infusion and warrants caution in sepsis.
indications: Supplementation of subpotent anesthetics (e.g., nitrous oxide) during short operative procedures
Rapid-sequence intubation induction where hemodynamic stability is desired (per labeling for induction; off-label emergency use is common)

dosage.d: 0.2-0.6 mg/kg IV over 30-60 seconds; usual 0.3 mg/kg
dosage.n: Dose individualized; titrate to clinical effect

dosage.d: Lower end of range; consider ~0.15-0.2 mg/kg
Smaller incremental IV doses during short procedures

admin: Inject into a large, fast-running vein to reduce injection pain and venous irritation
Have airway management and resuscitation equipment immediately available
Administer only by personnel trained in anesthesia/airway management
Do not use as a continuous infusion for sedation due to adrenal suppression
moa: Etomidate is a GABA-A receptor positive allosteric modulator that enhances chloride conductance and produces rapid hypnosis with minimal effect on cardiovascular function. It also reversibly inhibits 11-beta-hydroxylase (and 17-alpha-hydroxylase), the adrenal steroidogenic enzymes, producing dose-dependent suppression of cortisol and aldosterone synthesis.

monitor: Blood pressure, heart rate and oxygenation continuously

preg: Etomidate crosses the placenta. Adequate well-controlled human studies are lacking; use during pregnancy only if the potential benefit justifies the potential risk. Neonatal depression may follow use near delivery.
lact: Limited data; a single induction dose results in minimal infant exposure. Many clinicians permit breastfeeding once the mother is awake and stable; a brief interruption may be considered.
renal: No specific renal dose adjustment is required for single induction doses; titrate to effect. Protein binding changes in uremia may slightly increase free drug.
hepatic: Hepatic impairment may prolong and intensify effects due to reduced metabolism and altered protein binding; use cautiously and consider a lower dose.

major: Other CNS depressants (opioids, benzodiazepines, volatile anesthetics) - additive sedation/respiratory depression
moderate: Fentanyl - may prolong etomidate elimination; reduce dose
Neuromuscular blockers - sequenced use during RSI
minor: Verapamil - reports of prolonged anesthesia/respiratory depression
interactions.food: Not applicable; patients are typically fasted for anesthesia.
interactions.alcohol: Chronic or acute alcohol use potentiates CNS depression; account for in dosing.
interactions.diagnostics: Suppresses serum cortisol/aldosterone; may confound adrenal (cortisol/ACTH stimulation) testing for hours after a dose.

common: Transient blood pressure and heart rate changes

monitoring: Continuous BP, ECG, heart rate and pulse oximetry during and after induction
Adrenal (cortisol) function if more than a single dose or in critically ill patients
counsel: You will be given this medicine through a vein to put you to sleep for a procedure
A brief pain or muscle twitching at the time of injection is common
Nausea after waking can occur and can be treated
Tell your anesthetist about any allergies or previous anesthesia problems
Do not drive or operate machinery for 24 hours after anesthesia
pk: Near-immediate CNS effect after rapid IV bolus
Store at 20-25 C (68-77 F); protect from freezing
pearls: Hemodynamically the most stable common IV induction agent - useful in trauma, cardiac disease and shock
Even a single induction dose causes transient adrenal suppression; avoid continuous infusion and weigh use carefully in sepsis
Myoclonus is common and can be reduced with a small opioid or benzodiazepine pretreatment
Pain on injection is lessened by a large vein and/or lidocaine pretreatment
Lacks analgesic properties - pair with analgesia for painful procedures
missed: Not applicable - etomidate is a single-use intravenous induction agent administered by an anesthesia provider, not a scheduled self-administered medication.
overdose: Excessive dosing causes deep CNS and respiratory depression, apnea and hypotension. There is no specific antidote; management is supportive with airway control, mechanical ventilation, oxygen and hemodynamic support. Monitor and supplement adrenal function if needed.
